findings.source_quote: in mandatis huius ingredere, quae dedi tibi, et poteris dominari omni nequitiae.
findings.english_quote: Preserve the shepherd’s stated authority, moral-change language and life/death consequences.
findings.issue: The theological metadata describes this unit as preserving life/death consequences, but the selected source contains no life/death assertion. Its stated consequences concern protection, success, and mastery over evil. The translation itself does not introduce the unsupported consequences.
findings.suggested_revision: Remove “and life/death consequences” from this unit’s metadata, or explicitly identify it as broader-context commentary rather than content of the selected passage.

findings.source_quote: et dic omnibus in magno honore esse eum et dignitate apud Dominum
findings.english_quote: Tell everyone that the Lord gives him great honor and dignity.
findings.issue: The source states that the shepherd has great honor and dignity before the Lord. The simplified edition changes this standing into an explicit act of bestowal by the Lord, adding agency not expressed in this clause.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed wording for fresh review: “Tell everyone that he has great honor and dignity before the Lord.”

findings.source_quote: et magnae potestatis eum praesidem esse et potentem in officio suo.
findings.english_quote: He has great authority and power in his work.
findings.issue: The rendering retains authority and power but omits the explicit description of the shepherd as a presiding official or overseer, expressed by praesidem. Possessing authority does not fully convey that stated role.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed wording for fresh review: “He is an overseer with great authority and is powerful in his role.”

findings.source_quote: maturitatem huius et modestiam suscipe in te
findings.issue: Suscipe in te directs the hearer to take these qualities into himself—to adopt them. “Learn” can mean acquiring knowledge of them without making them one's own, weakening the directive to internalize the qualities.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed wording for fresh review: “Make his patience and restraint your own.[a]” Retain the disclosed lexical qualification concerning maturitas.

findings.source_quote: in mandatis huius ingredere, quae dedi tibi, et poteris dominari omni nequitiae.
findings.english_quote: Preserve the shepherd’s stated authority, moral-change language and life/death consequences.
findings.issue: The theological metadata attributes life/death consequences to this unit, although none are expressed in the selected source. The passage instead states consequences involving protection, success, and mastery over evil.
findings.suggested_revision: Remove “and life/death consequences” from this unit’s metadata, or clearly label it as broader-context commentary.

findings.source_quote: huic soli per totum orbem paenitentiae potestas tributa est.
findings.english_quote: Shorter sentences preserve the shepherd’s authority, ethical scope, blood-guilt and remedy language, and all noted alternatives.
findings.issue: The simplification metadata claims to preserve blood-guilt and remedy language that does not occur in this selected unit. This is an inaccurate account of what the edition simplifies, even though such language has not been inserted into its reader text.
findings.suggested_revision: Replace the scope description with one limited to this passage, such as preserving the dialogue, ethical scope, shepherd’s authority, and disclosed lexical alternatives. Any replacement requires fresh review.

summary: Both editions were reviewed against the complete supplied Latin unit. The standard reader text covers its clauses faithfully; revision is needed for inaccurate metadata. The simplified edition additionally introduces divine bestowal, omits the explicit presiding role, and weakens the instruction to adopt the shepherd’s qualities. Contextual “repentance” and the disclosed maturitas reading are compatible with current policy. The supplied reports support the stated exclusion of Amherst coverage for this unit; no unseen manuscript, edition, or exhaustive collation is certified.
